text:
sanjay: Heads up — kernel rollout to 6.3 started in eu-west2 ~10:30 UTC and we're seeing P4 hosts go into OOM/reboot loops and NVIDIA modules failing to load. NCCL handshakes timing out for a bunch of pods. creating thread to coordinate.

maria: ugh. which image/tag did the rollout use? any pattern across instance types?

sanjay: it was the k6-3-ga image (rolling from 5.15). affected mostly p4d and p4d-2 nodes, a few p4s. symptoms: modprobe failures, then processes dying with SIGSEGV in nvidia. logs pasted below.

kevin: paste dmesg/log snippet?

sanjay: ```
[  132.451234] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[  132.451245] nvidia: Unknown symbol nvidia_gpu_init (err -2)
[  133.112345] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[  140.998765] oom-killer: kill process 1624 (python) score 958 or sacrifice child
[  142.001234] kernel: RIP: 0010:__nvidia_alloc@/build/nvidia/nvidia.ko+0x1f2c
``` 

ellie: looks like unresolved symbol / ABI mismatch between nvidia.ko and kernel. maybe driver build flags or header mismatch.

maria: are we shipping NVIDIA driver via dkms or baked into AMI?

sanjay: drivers are baked into the golden image for these fleets (CUDA 11.8 + nvidia 525.x). DKMS is disabled for perf reasons.

kevin: CUDA 11.8 + driver 525 should be fine on 6.x in general, but we have a custom kernel config (CONFIG_MODVERSIONS off, some LTO flags) — possible ABI issue. Also saw earlier that build system signed modules with a key not in the 6.3 RT system keyring.

oncall: infra-bot created INC-2026-001 and pinned affected hosts. alerting on provisioning backlog in eu-west2: 48 pending pods waiting for GPU scheduling.

infra-bot: [incident created] INC-2026-001 — kernel 6.3 rollout causing nvidia module incompat / host instability. Priority: P1. Runbook: cordon, drain, rollback image if >5 hosts fail in region.

ellie: suggested immediate mitigation: cordon affected hosts, set fleet autoscaler to avoid replacing them with same image, and scale up fallback pool (5.15 nodes) if available.

maria: can we fast rollback AMI? image pipeline supports quick revert but time to reprovision ~12-15m per node. capacity wise eu-west2 only has 40 spare p4 slots across reserved pools.

sanjay: current numbers: 23 hosts unhealthy, 48 pending pods. If we revert those 23 to the 5.15 image it'll take ~4.6 hours sequentially; we can parallelize to 8 at a time but that'll spike API calls and increase provisioning cost.

kevin: short term: patch kube-scheduler to prefer fallback node groups with known-good kernels and blacklist the k6-3 pool. I'll open a scheduler-pr to deprioritize label:kernel=6.3.

ellie: also recommend toggling fast-fallback routing in the serving runtime so LBs drain connections off affected nodes (reduce NCCL handshake failures).

maria: any chance to rebuild nvidia modules against 6.3 and push as hotfix instead of changing images? we could build signed modules matching kernel config and scp/install.

sanjay: hotfix path is possible but risky: we'd have to build and sign modules for our custom config and test. timeframe ~2-3 hours to build + quick soak. risk to scale.

oncall: what's the team decision? rollback image, hotfix, or wait? we need to commit in next 15m.

kevin: vote: rollback image for affected pools (safer), AND start parallel build of signed modules as contingency. rollback reduces immediate risk to production traffic.

ellie: +1 rollback + hotfix build. I'll coordinate rollout windows and throttle to 8 nodes at a time.

maria: I'll trigger image rollback and update terraform to pin the nodepool config. starting now.

sanjay: executing cordon/drain commands for the 23 failing hosts now:

sanjay: ```
for n in $(cat failed-hosts.txt); do kubectl cordon $n && kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force &
done
```

kevin: I'll open capacity ticket with cloud provider to request temporary burst quota in eu-west2 for p4s if rollback triggers lots of reprovisioning.

infra-bot: [note] autoscaler disabled for k6-3 pool at 1850004350.

maria: rollback jobs started (batch of 6 nodes). monitoring progress in the rollout dashboard.

ellie: added alert: NCCL handshake error rate > 5% -> page oncall.

oncall: thanks all. keep updates here. once rollback finishes we'll evaluate whether to resume 6.3 canary after signed module build and compatibility tests.

sanjay: summary: rollback underway, hotfix build queued, incident INC-2026-001 active. expecting recovery window 2-4h depending on parallelism. :thumbsup:
